races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Race

runners_data.name: Bold Style
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery's stable companion to Loughrea, Bold Style is a natural hold-up horse who needs the race run to suit; 178 days off the track is a concern, and while her best form at 8f on Good ground is encouraging, the likely moderate pace set by Res Ipsa may not bring her finishing kick into play.

runners_data.name: Loughrea
runners_data.note: In good recent form with a win and a place over 8f on Good ground in her last two starts, Loughrea is genuinely a horse that wants to race prominently, but with Res Ipsa dominating that position she will likely find herself racing further back than ideal — a positional compromise that tempers her chance.

runners_data.name: Res Ipsa
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front runner, trained by G M Lyons and ridden by Colin Keane, Res Ipsa has won and placed over 8f on Good ground and, with no meaningful challenger for the lead, is set to control every phase of this race at her own pace — a significant tactical advantage.

runners_data.name: Straight Up
runners_data.note: Wayne Lordan partners this A P O'Brien hold-up horse who has struggled to convert prominent finishes into wins on Good going, with no wins recorded in four similar-ground starts; at OR 99 she has the class but her form figures suggest a horse that finds a way to get beaten, and a slow pace is no help.

runners_data.name: Mai Dahlia
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's consistent filly arrives on the back of three consecutive placings-or-wins over 8-10f on Good turf and is the freshest runner in the field at 9 days since her last start; she wears headgear (tongue tie) and Dylan Browne McMonagle's booking is significant — she is the most likely horse to press Res Ipsa and reverse form if the front runner is not fully at peak.

races.paceDynamic: Res Ipsa is the confirmed front runner and, with only Mai Dahlia capable of pressing from a prominent position, she is likely to set a controlled, sustainable gallop over this mile at Killarney. Mai Dahlia will sit close behind, but neither Bold Style nor Straight Up are natural pace-pressers, meaning Res Ipsa should dictate tempo without serious challenge. The field contains more prominent-types than the map can accommodate — Loughrea is a genuine prominent racer who is unlikely to secure that berth and has been redistributed to midfield, while Res Ipsa and Mai Dahlia will likely monopolise the front positions. A steady-to-modest pace set by Res Ipsa on Good turf over a mile favours horses with tactical versatility and a clean turn of foot at the business end — prominent runners who can control the race without burning fuel, rather than deep closers who will need a genuine test to get involved.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Res Ipsa Controls, Kicks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Res Ipsa bowls along uncontested at a comfortable clip and quickens entering the straight.
scenarios.body: Res Ipsa sets honest but untroubled fractions, building a buffer that hold-up horses cannot bridge in time; Mai Dahlia, sitting just off her heels, is ideally placed to chase but must match a winner who has not been emptied by pressure.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Mai Dahlia applies sustained pressure to Res Ipsa from the home turn, turning it into a two-horse battle.
scenarios.body: The tempo lifts significantly in the final quarter-mile as the two prominent types battle heads apart, leaving the hold-up horses with ground to make up but a stronger gallop to close into; Mai Dahlia's recent winning form and fitness edge gives her the advantage if she can wear down Res Ipsa.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so slow early that the field bunches and a sprint develops, gifting hold-up horses a chance.
scenarios.body: Bold Style and Straight Up, both hold-up operators, find themselves no worse positioned than usual in a compressed field; Bold Style's best form at this trip and on Good ground makes her the logical closer beneficiary if the gaps open in the straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Loughrea Defies Redistribution
scenarios.trigger: If the race breaks slowly enough that Loughrea can push forward to reclaim a prominent position close to the leaders.
scenarios.body: Loughrea — a genuine prominent type — has strong recent form including a win and second on Good ground at this trip; if she can get cover just off the pace rather than being buried in midfield, her class over these rivals at OR 86 makes her dangerous.

watchPoints.text: Res Ipsa sets the entire pace dynamic — watch her early sections; if Colin Keane elects to dawdle, the race compresses and hold-up horses Bold Style and Straight Up gain a route back into contention.

Loughrea's natural inclination to race prominently means Andrew Slattery may attempt to push her forward regardless — watch the early furlong to see if she can secure a position better than her mapped midfield slot.
Mai Dahlia ran only 9 days ago; watch her in the paddock for any signs of training stress, as a tired horse pressing Res Ipsa from the front could unravel rather than threaten.

Bold Style's 178-day absence means her first show of pace in the straight will be instructive — if she hits the front swiftly she is fit and dangerous; if she struggles to quicken the layoff has taken its toll.

races.name: SIS Supporting Irish Racing Handicap

runners_data.name: Red Autumn
runners_data.note: D K Weld's hold-up filly has placed on good and similar going and Sam Coen's 5lb claim is an asset; her best form is at 7-8f which suits the trip, though she needs the pace to be honest enough to make her late run count from the back.

runners_data.name: Johnny Soda
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with a win at 8f on good going in recent form; Adam Caffrey takes the ride for a trainer running at 2/29 in 14 days, and his role as sole pace-setter is his clearest asset, though he is effectively racing out of his most efficient role as a pure leader in this wide-open handicap.

runners_data.name: Golddream
runners_data.note: David Marnane's gelding won at 8f on standard going and has placed on good; Luke McAteer partners him at the top of the weights and his prominent style suits a race where he can travel in Johnny Soda's slipstream without expending energy.

runners_data.name: Glitter And Glory
runners_data.note: Mrs John Harrington's filly boasts the strongest placed record in the field on good ground (5 runs, two places), handles this trip well and Nathan Crosse keeps the ride; consistent without winning lately but her tactical versatility makes her competitive across most scenarios.

runners_data.name: Vishaya
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's filly carries an unresolved style rating (U) and Dylan Browne McMonagle — one of the in-form jockeys in Ireland — is a significant positive; her best of three runs came at 8f on good, and the O'Brien yard is firing with 14/53 in 14 days which demands attention.

runners_data.name: Casamorati
runners_data.note: The 69-day absence is a notable flag, and her last three runs show a consistent pattern of fading late which undermines her chances in any scenario; Declan McDonogh partners for the same powerful O'Brien yard but her hold-up style and finishing tendency make her the most vulnerable runner in the field.

runners_data.name: Chirac
runners_data.note: John James Feane's gelding is a genuine prominent racer by nature, with a recent win at 8f on good and placed form in that going band, but the crowded prominent berths mean he is likely pushed wider in the field than he'd like; Ronan Whelan will need to navigate traffic to get any value from his natural speed.

runners_data.name: Dervo Annie
runners_data.note: Claire O'Connell's filly arrives on a quick 12-day turnaround with a win at 6f on good and placed form at 7f; she is naturally front-running in style and the compressed prominent group means she faces the same problem as Chirac — her best chance exists only if she can bully her way to a position she may not obtain.

races.paceDynamic: Johnny Soda is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger likely to press him from the jump, he should control tempo from the front at a measured, sustainable gallop over this flat mile at Killarney. Golddream and Glitter And Glory are the other true prominent types best placed to track him through the early stages, while Dervo Annie and Chirac — both natural front-runners by style — are likely to find themselves racing out of their preferred role and sitting further back than ideal given the volume of prominent pace in this field. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can comfortably accommodate; of those, Johnny Soda is overwhelmingly most likely to actually secure the lead, with Golddream and Glitter And Glory the next most likely to get close to the pace. A steady, uncontested gallop set by Johnny Soda strongly favours horses who can travel prominently and quicken, or closers with a genuine late gear, but the key tactical verdict is that a controlled pace benefits hold-up horses only if they carry a true finishing kick — those like Red Autumn who have demonstrated ability to close from off the pace on similar ground are the profile to watch.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Johnny Soda Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Johnny Soda leads unchallenged and sets a steady, even gallop that plays to his strengths.
scenarios.body: Johnny Soda dictates from the front, keeps the tempo honest but not dawdling, and holds enough in reserve to repel challengers; Golddream and Glitter And Glory travel smoothly in his wake and are well-placed to pounce if he ties up. Prominent trackers are the clear beneficiaries of this shape, able to conserve energy while never being out of the race.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace compresses the field and leaves genuine late finishers with energy to unleash a run from off the bridle in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Red Autumn, racing from hold-up as her natural style, would be the main beneficiary if the pace is just honest enough to string out the field without burning up the leaders; she has placed on similar going and McAteer on Golddream could also finish with purpose. This scenario requires the pace to be more than a dawdle, otherwise the leaders simply coast home.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Johnny Soda goes far too steady and the race degenerates into a bunched sprint in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A crawl would neutralise hold-up runners and put a premium on raw speed in a tight, tactical finish, favouring whoever has the best turn of foot; Glitter And Glory's multiple placed form at up to a mile and Golddream's wins at this trip make them live candidates in this shape. Dervo Annie and Chirac, despite their out-of-role mapping, could also benefit if they manage to get closer to the pace than expected and unleash natural speed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Fractures, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Dervo Annie or Chirac push forward and force a contested early gallop that stretches the field and burns out the prominently placed.
scenarios.body: A genuinely hot pace would tire the leaders and open the door for hold-up horses like Red Autumn and Casamorati — though Casamorati's tendency to fade late is a significant concern. Red Autumn, who has form placing off the pace, would be the primary beneficiary if stamina becomes the decisive factor over this flat mile.

watchPoints.text: Johnny Soda's ability to control tempo unchallenged is the single biggest swing factor — if Dervo Annie or Chirac push forward early, the entire race shape changes and prominently placed horses could be caught in a battle they cannot sustain.

Casamorati's 69-day layoff combined with a consistent record of fading in the finish makes her a significant late-race liability; watch for her to drop away in the final furlong regardless of scenario.

Vishaya's unresolved running style (tagged U) means Dylan Browne McMonagle's early positioning decision will be crucial — she could slot anywhere from prominent to midfield and her true pace profile only becomes clear in the first two furlongs.

Red Autumn's claim jockey Sam Coen (5lb) removes a meaningful weight burden at 141lbs; monitor whether she is able to find daylight in the straight, as her hold-up profile requires a clear passage that a bunched field may not provide.

The trainer form for Joseph Patrick O'Brien (14/53 in 14 days) means both Vishaya and Casamorati deserve respect on market signals — if one of them is heavily supported pre-race, it likely reflects stable confidence rather than the form alone.

races.name: Killarney Glamping Handicap

runners_data.name: Howyoulikethat
runners_data.note: A thorough hold-up operator for Miss Hilary McLoughlin, returning after 115 days off, whose best recent effort was a third at this trip on Flat-equivalent ground — needs a slow pace and a clear outside passage in the straight; 0W1P in similar going suggests he places more than wins.

runners_data.name: American Lawyer
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and returning from a huge 335-day absence for A J Martin, whose 14-day strike rate is 1/8, making fitness the central question; running style is genuinely unknown, which adds risk but also upside if the handicapper has not seen his ceiling.

runners_data.name: Quatre Bras
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone front-runner for Richard John O'Brien, whose 14-day return is a modest 0/2 and whose historic form at similar going reads 0W0P in one run — the style fit score of 0.92 signals he is racing in an unnatural prominent role, but the absence of any rival for the lead means he gets it by default regardless.

runners_data.name: Earls
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's veteran has solid placed form at this trip on good ground (two seconds at 8f/GOO recently), and although his natural instinct is to come from off the pace, congestion at the rear means he is likely to end up in a tracking midfield role — the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 tempers expectations slightly.

runners_data.name: Molto Amichi
runners_data.note: Eoin Griffin's five-year-old has a strong placed record at 0W5P in similar going, operating as a prominent racer who travels well off a steady pace; the worry is a step back to 8f from his last few outings at 9-10f, though the form at 8f-9f is reasonable.

runners_data.name: Louiescall
runners_data.note: Returning after 268 days off for David Harry Kelly, who has not placed a runner from 11 attempts in the past fortnight — Louiescall's best form at Good ground over longer trips (1W6P at 15-16f) raises an obvious question about whether a mile is short enough to see his stamina deployed optimally.

runners_data.name: Marta's Prince
runners_data.note: R P Burns's four-year-old is fresh from a 13-day turnaround and has limited similar-going evidence (0W0P in one relevant run); a hold-up profile and modest recent form string including a zero last time mean he needs significant improvement from these rivals.

runners_data.name: Grey Leader
runners_data.note: Stable companion to Marta's Prince, also 13 days since last run for Burns, and carrying a deeply unconvincing recent record of 0-0080 — naturally a hold-up runner, he has been pushed into a mapped midfield slot by the volume of deep closers in this field, and his 1W1P in similar going came over a different trip on different ground conditions entirely.

races.paceDynamic: Quatre Bras is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should coast into a comfortable, uncontested position from the outset, dictating a steady, controlled gallop over this mile on good turf. Molto Amichi and Louiescall will press forward into prominent positions behind the pacesetter, creating a compact front group but no meaningful pressure on Quatre Bras. Grey Leader and Earls are true hold-up horses by nature who are mapped into midfield positions because the field carries more deep closers than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — of the redistributed pair, Earls has the stronger recent placed form and is likeliest to secure a workable tracking position, while Grey Leader's poor recent figures make a midfield slot from which to launch a challenge uncertain. With a lone, uncontested leader setting a sustainable tempo and two genuine prominents travelling just behind, this shape strongly favours hold-up horses with a turn of foot who can be produced wide in the straight, and secondarily those prominent types capable of quickening off a modest pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Quatre Bras Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Quatre Bras leads unchallenged at a steady tempo, the race sets up as a one-act sprint home.
scenarios.body: Quatre Bras sets fractions entirely to his own liking and the field strings out in a measured line, leaving prominent types like Molto Amichi and Louiescall travelling comfortably just behind but unable to pressurise the leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is slow enough that the field concertinas and a finisher can produce a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: A crawl in front means horses are still in a bunch past halfway, and any hold-up runner who gets a clear outside run in the final two furlongs can pick off the tiring front group.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Type Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fractionally stronger than expected and Quatre Bras pays for it late, leaving a prominent chaser to inherit the prize.
scenarios.body: Molto Amichi or Louiescall, travelling smoothly just off the fractions, moves to challenge inside the final furlong as Quatre Bras weakens, with no hold-up horse having enough momentum to peg them back.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lightly Raced Type Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If American Lawyer, fresh off a 335-day absence, has trained into full fitness and exploits a flat handicap mark on unknown potential.
scenarios.body: American Lawyer, lightly raced and unexposed at this trip with a stable that placed one recent runner from eight, produces a one-off performance that punishes the field's exposed form.

watchPoints.text: Quatre Bras leads unchallenged from the gate — if W J Lee is allowed to dictate an artificially slow tempo into the final turn, all hold-up types are flattered but the race may be over before they land a blow.

Grey Leader and Earls are both natural hold-up horses squeezed into midfield on the map — watch the early stages for both jockeys angling wide to avoid traffic, as a bunched field could cause interference if they both seek the same gap.
Louiescall's 268-day absence combined with David Harry Kelly's 0/11 trainer strike rate over the past fortnight is a significant fitness flag — monitor paddock condition closely before the off.

American Lawyer (335 days absent, unknown style) is the biggest wildcard in the field — if A J Martin has prepared this horse specifically for this race, the absence of any recent form makes it very difficult for the market to price him accurately.

Howyoulikethat's 5lb claim for Sam Coen could prove meaningful if the pace is genuinely slow and he gets a clean run from off the pace — his 0W1P record in similar conditions suggests a place rather than a win, but weight matters late in a handicap.

races.name: Kerry Publicans Summer Race Day Fillies Maiden
Irish Stallion Farms EBF Median Auction Maiden
Heights Hotel, Killarney Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: Sands Castle
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3yo with course-relevant Good-ground form (placed at 10f/Good most recently) and a claiming apprentice allowance in the saddle; hold-up style means she needs the pace to be genuine enough to deliver her from off it.|

runners_data.name: Sir Trancealot
runners_data.note: Ben Coen takes the ride for the in-form J P Murtagh yard (7/32 over 14 days) and his last three runs are all at 12f or beyond on Good, making the trip very suitable; genuine hold-up horse who will need traffic to part.|

runners_data.name: Wipeawayyourtears
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in this race and the sole pace anchor — wearing a hood, she won over 12f Good last time and steps up slightly in trip; her STYLE_FIT score reflects that she is slightly out of her natural comfort zone heading to a bigger field.|

runners_data.name: Chicago Moon
runners_data.note: De Bromhead representative who is a genuine hold-up horse by record, placed here in midfield purely by the weight of closers in this field; his single Good-ground placing came at 10f and he has been off 62 days.|

runners_data.name: Point Cartwright
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with two placed efforts at 11-12f on Good this season; Ronan Whelan takes the mount and this horse's natural style fits the race shape well — one of the few who genuinely wants to race close to a slow pace.|

runners_data.name: Guildhall Graduate
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell handler carries modest strike rate over 14 days (1/46); a true hold-up horse whose form at distance beyond a mile is uninspiring, shifted to midfield on the map only because the rear is oversubscribed — not a natural on-pace type.|

runners_data.name: Cameclose
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading finishes and a genuine hold-up horse by inclination, appearing in midfield on the map because of field congestion at the rear; James Ryan can't change the horse's tendency to stop late.|

runners_data.name: Flagstone Lady
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the mount but her form reads bleak — multiple teens finishes on Good this season, fading flag attached, and she is a hold-up type nudged into midfield rather than the rear simply by the volume of closers in this race.|

runners_data.name: Tintinabulla
runners_data.note: Modest form in three career runs, all showing finishing weakness; trips of 10-12f on Soft or Good with no placing, and as a genuine hold-up type she is one of the few correctly placed at the rear of the map.|

runners_data.name: Augusta Rock
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's runner hasn't placed in four starts and wears a visor; DBM takes the ride but the horse has been off 71 days and form in soft-ground suggests Good may suit better in theory — still a true hold-up type pushed midfield by field volume.|

runners_data.name: No Bother Aoife
runners_data.note: A tongue-tie adds a small angle for Gavin Cromwell, and she placed at 12f/Good most recently — but her fade flag and hold-up tendencies mean she must thread through horses that have also been compressed into midfield.|

runners_data.name: Polanco
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie fitted but form is alarming — multiple last-place finishes including 15th of 15 twice; a genuine closer by record mapped to midfield because the hold-up quarter is full, but no evidence of the engine needed to exploit this trip.|

runners_data.name: Stonyfalls
runners_data.note: Placed third in a 3f-shorter race at Galway on Good recently, which is form worth noting; fade flag is a concern at the longer trip, and as a natural hold-up type correctly seated at the rear, she needs a strongly-run race.|

runners_data.name: Cadreville
runners_data.note: Neve Bennett (7lb claim) is a notable booking; Good-ground form includes a place at 10f and a third at 11f, and stepping up to 11½f may suit — a true closer mapped to midfield by congestion, not by preference.|

runners_data.name: Canon Law
runners_data.note: A Flat card full of Good-ground form but all on Stable going (AW), making this turf assignment a significant unknown; hold-up type nudged to midfield by the volume of closers behind the pace, and trainer has modest recent numbers (0/3 over 14 days).|

races.paceDynamic: Wipeawayyourtears is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 15-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine pace rival to force the issue — she should dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset over this 1m3½f trip, creating a race that flows rhythmically rather than frantically. Point Cartwright and Sands Castle may attempt to track closely from prominent positions, but the absence of any rival willing or able to challenge Wipeawayyourtears for the lead means the fractions will be dictated entirely on her terms. This field is heavily stacked with hold-up types — Polanco, No Bother Aoife, Guildhall Graduate, Chicago Moon, Flagstone Lady and others are genuine closers by nature but have been mapped to midfield simply because the rear of the field cannot accommodate them all, meaning traffic and positional disadvantage late will be a real factor for many. A controlled pace set by a lone leader on Good turf over a staying trip historically favours horses who can travel prominently, sit just off the pace, and produce a sustained gallop rather than a sharp late burst — the race shape here squarely favours prominent racers and those with the stamina to reel in a front-runner who has controlled their own energy.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Wipeawayyourtears Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Wipeawayyourtears establishes an uncontested lead and dictates a moderate gallop that saps the stamina of the chasing pack.
scenarios.body: She sets her own fractions, conserves energy through the middle mile, and kicks clear when challenged approaching the straight, leaving hold-up horses with too much ground to make up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Runs Her Down
scenarios.trigger: If a horse tracking in second or third moves alongside Wipeawayyourtears entering the straight and sustains the challenge to the line.
scenarios.body: The pace being controlled rather than strong means a horse travelling easily just behind the leader has every chance to collar her in the final furlong without needing a sharp sprint.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Weaves Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sufficiently in the straight to stretch and expose the leader and prominently-placed horses, enabling a horse from further back to close ground.
scenarios.body: For this to materialise a true closer must avoid traffic from a field bunched by moderate fractions — the redistributed nature of most hold-up types mapped to midfield makes a clean run far from guaranteed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Swamps Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Wipeawayyourtears stops suddenly late having gone too hard in front, triggering a blanket finish from the chasing group.
scenarios.body: A moderate collapse of the leader benefits horses who have travelled well in the first half of the race and have residual energy — those with finishing-fade flags are at risk of also tying up.

watchPoints.text: Wipeawayyourtears has the race by the throat from the front — watch whether Jack Cleary (5) controls the fractions sensibly or allows the 15-runner field to push her faster than she wants in the early stages.

Point Cartwright and Sir Trancealot are the two horses most likely to sit closest to the leader and produce a sustained challenge — if either can get a clean passage into the straight without covering extra ground, they become dangerous.

The sheer volume of hold-up horses mapped to midfield — including Guildhall Graduate, Chicago Moon, No Bother Aoife and Polanco — creates a serious traffic risk in the straight; watch for interference between the 2f and 1f poles.
Sands Castle's apprentice claim (Harry Sexton, 7lb) could be significant if the race cuts up and she gets a clear run from the rear — but she needs things to go wrong for those ahead of her.
Augusta Rock has been off 71 days under Dylan Browne McMonagle — watch her market move in the final hour as a market springer off a rest could be significant despite uninspiring recent form.
